strategy.summary: Family-owned German investment/steel foundry (founded 1962, 160 staff, sound finances, our spend is a small share of its turnover) supplying the volute casing 310050 (A-part, the larger share against a CZ second source) and the impeller 310051 (the larger share against a CN second source) under a framework agreement with yearly fixed prices, a notice rule for price changes and auto-renewal. Leverage is ours. We own the tooling on both parts, both parts are dual-sourced with cheaper rivals, the impeller sits far above a (low-confidence, CN-based) should-cost, and delivery reliability is poor and worsening. Volume forecasts are rising. The owner has just visited, recalled a past price hold and asked for partnership in return. Expect a modest increase request built on alloy surcharge and labour. History shows it asks roughly flat and settles below its ask. The volute casing has an excellent quality record and the CZ rival has a poor one, so it is the part we least want to lose. The impeller is the weak part on delivery and quality.

persona.style: Owner-led, relationship and reciprocity minded. Written communication is sparse and operational. Historically cooperative in renewals, settling below its ask.

Delivery capability is weak and has never come near the contractual target. Confirmed dates slip against requested dates, which may point to tight capacity on the impeller.
The supplier is not dependent on us and is financially stable, so excessive pressure risks it walking away, especially on the volute casing where the alternative source has poor quality.

Prefer fixed prices because the drivers move modestly. Accept an alloy-only clause only if demanded, priced well below the fixed price.

price_view.reasoning: The net driver movement is small and the alloy surcharge is already falling back. The impeller is far above should-cost and the rival price, so there is real room there. On the casing, room exists against the CZ rival, but our tool-owning switch threat is weakened by the rival's quality. Its history is to settle below its ask. An increase is not justified beyond token recognition; aim for flat to a modest cut, mainly on the impeller.

strategy.writer_notes: Open warmly, recognising the owner's visit and the earlier price hold. Offer real partnership: a longer commitment, binding volume where our need is firm, and a commitment to pay on time. Put the pressure mainly on the impeller using the should-cost benchmark. Keep the casing gentler because its quality is excellent and we need it. Answer any increase claim with the recent alloy fall and power decline, and with the contractual notice rule if the timing is late. Hold delivery and quality records as later fresh facts.

findings.text: Impeller 310051: price EUR 118.73 is +39.7% over the bottom-up should-cost of EUR 84.97. That estimate is for the CN plant of sup:70160 and excludes margin, so it overstates the gap for a German foundry. Its confidence is only 5%. Even after a fair margin and a DE cost premium, the evidence points to price room, not to an increase.

Volute casing 310050 has no should-cost. Cost economics can only be inferred from rival prices. sup:70170 (CZ) supplies the same part at EUR 559.61 (-14.5%) and quoted EUR 598.10 in the 2025 RFQ, against Allgäu-Reiter's 676.60 and its current 654.52.

Impeller 310051 rival gap: Meridune (CN) pays-in at EUR 79.44 and quoted 91.40 in 2024, against Allgäu-Reiter's 130.30 then and 118.73 now. The rival's lead time is 112 days versus 48, and its payment term is 90 days, so part of the gap is a logistics and working-capital difference, not margin.

Weighted driver movement over 12 months nets to roughly +1.9% on cost for both parts:
- labour +2.7% at weight 0.26-0.29
- alloy surcharge +5.9% at weight 0.24
- power -3.7% at weight 0.06-0.09
This is modest, and the alloy surcharge has already fallen about 5.5% since 2026-06. A small increase claim is checkable, but it is far smaller than the price-to-cost and rival gaps.

Since the last price (2026-01) the changes are:
- labour and the alloy surcharge are up
- power is down
- volume forecast is up about 13% on 310050 and about 5% on 310051

The supplier will likely cite market news on copper, electronics and steel. Those do not match its drivers (1.4408 cast steel), and iron castings are only +1.8%.
Price history: cuts each renewal (-5.7% on 310050 and -9.3% on 310051 since 2023), and it habitually settles 2-3 pp below its ask. The supplier will frame these cuts as concessions already given.

findings.text: Decision-maker is the owner of a family-owned firm (founded 1962, 160 staff). He came in person on 2026-09-24 and appealed to the relationship: in 2022 they kept supplying at the old price for a quarter, and he expects partnership in return. This reads as setting up a price-increase or renewal request on a personal, reciprocity footing. Acknowledging the 2022 gesture explicitly is likely to matter more to him than numbers alone.

Financially sound and stable. Equity ratio is 25%, the credit index is unchanged at 244 over 12 months, and turnover is EUR 24.1M. Our spend of about EUR 0.8M is only about 3.3% of its turnover, so it is not dependent on us and can afford to walk away. No sign of financial stress, so a cash or liquidity lever is weak.

Our payment behaviour is a sensitivity he can raise. 91.4% of invoices are paid late, on average 4.4 days after due in the last 12 months (max 11), and this is on terms of only 30 days. In a 'partnership' framing, on-time or faster payment is a cheap give for us.

Its own performance weakens its position. On-time delivery is 73.1% against a 95% target, down from 80.0% a year earlier and below the peer median of 84.6%. Quality is 526 ppm against a peer median of 457, with one 8D overdue (missing marking on part 310051). Partnership cuts both ways.

Historically cooperative pattern: across 3 renewals per part it asked roughly flat and settled 2-3% lower, and prices fell 5.7% (310050) and 9.3% (310051) since 2023. It may now feel it has given enough and use that history together with the 2022 gesture as its argument.
Its communication style is sparse: we hold only a short operational e-mail (returnable boxes from November 2025) and one meeting note. The evidence on persona is thin.

findings.text: Framework agreement runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30, auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice (by 2027-04-01). Exit is still open and credible, which gives us leverage in any renewal.
Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, so by about 2 Oct 2026 for 2027. A late increase request has no contractual basis for 1 Jan.

Payment is 30 days net against our 60-day standard, so they already enjoy fast payment. We pay on average 4.4 days late (91% of invoices late), which they can raise against us. Incoterm is FCA, with a 49-day lead time.

The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per complaint. Actual on-time delivery is 73.1% (a year earlier 80%), well below target. The single complaint on 310051 has not been recharged and its 8D is still open.

History: in all three renewals per part they settled below their ask. Average gap is 1.7 pp on 310050 and 2.8 pp on 310051, with 0 to -6.4% price changes each year. Prices fell 5.7% and 9.3% since 2023. The supplier concedes readily, but the owner now invokes 2022 'partnership'.

Dependency is low on both sides. We own the tooling for both parts, and both parts are dual-sourced: CZ 25% on 310050 and CN 40% on 310051. The rival prices are much lower: 310050 at 559.61 vs 654.52, and 310051 at 79.44 vs 118.73. Our spend is about 3.3% of their turnover. They won both benchmark RFQs, though, and are financially sound.

findings.text: Delivery is the weak spot: rolling 12-month OTD fell to 73.1% vs requested (78.8% vs its own confirmed dates) against a 95% contract target; a year earlier 80.0%. Late deliveries average 14.5 days, max 31. Score dropped from 88 (A, green) in 2026Q1 to 78.9 (B, amber) in 2026Q3. OTD has never exceeded 81.5% in nine quarters.

Impeller part:310051 is the worse performer: 66.7% on time vs requested, 29.6% late; all 3 QNs of this supplier are on this part (dimension, wrong certificate, missing marking). The 2026-07-18 QN still has no closed 8D (open_8d_overdue 1). Only EUR 150 recharged in total.

Volute casing part:310050: zero defects on 1055 pcs in 12 months (rival sup:70170 had 5682 ppm), but 20% late with 18.2 days average lateness. Quality argues its case on this part; delivery argues ours.
Quality trend improving overall: rolling ppm 1133 a year ago down to 526, though still above the peer median 457; only 1 complaint, so the figure is jumpy.

Volume outlook rises: 310050 forecast 1593 vs 1406 ordered (+13%), 310051 1483 vs 1408 (+5%), both shared with the supplier. Our ordered qty from this supplier on 310050 was 983 of ~1406 (quota ~70-75%). Growth is a trade chip for price or for binding OTD commitments.

Prices well above parallel sources on same parts: 310050 at 654.52 vs sup:70170 559.61 (-14.5%); 310051 at 118.73 vs sup:70160 79.44 (-33%) and should-cost 84.97. Order history shows steady small cuts (-5.7% / -9.3% since 2023), which it will cite.
Its side: recent POs all confirmed on requested date, returnable boxes introduced, owner invoked 2022 price hold; we pay 4.4 days late on average (91% of invoices).

arguments.text: Volute casing quality is flawless while the alternative is not: zero complaints on 310050 over 1,055 parts received in the last 12 months, against 5,682 ppm at the Czech second source. Our price buys avoided defects and line stoppages, and switching quota to the cheaper source costs Hollerau more than the price gap.

Partnership and history. In 2022 we held the old price for a quarter, and the owner raised this in person. Since then we have given back every year: -3.7%/-6.4% in 2024, flat in 2025 even though we had asked for +1.5%/+4%, and -2.1%/-3% in 2026. Our casing price is down 5.7% and our impeller price 9.3% since 2023, so we have already passed on more than the market moved.

Cost drivers are rising, not falling. The alloy surcharge for 1.4404 is +5.9% year on year and weighs about 24%. Manufacturing labour is +2.7% and at its peak, weighing 26-29%. Steel is +7.3% since January. Only power fell (-3.7%), and its weight is just 6-9%. On net this is roughly +2% of cost pressure, so a further cut is unjustified and holding flat is already a concession.

The impeller should-cost is built on a Chinese plant at 5% confidence and includes no margin. It is not a benchmark for a German foundry. The CN source quoted 112 days of lead time and needed 10 rush lines; we quoted 48 days.
Payment discipline. Hollerau pays 91.4% of our invoices late, on average 4.4 days over an already short 30-day term. Faster, punctual payment has value to us.
Contractually, prices are fixed per calendar year and auto-renew. A price cut is not owed either; it is a negotiation.

weak_points: Delivery is poor: 73.1% on time in the last 12 months against the 95% target, and the impeller is at 66.7%. Lateness averages 14.5 days and has reached 31 days.
The scorecard has dropped to class B / amber (78.9), with an overdue 8D on qn:20004976 that is still open.
Three impeller complaints in a row, including a wrong material certificate and a missing marking.
Our impeller costs 118.73 against 79.44 from the CN source (+49%), and we are about 40% above the should-cost.
Our casing costs 654.52 against 559.61 from the CZ source (+17%), and our 2025 quote was 676.6 against 598.1.
Hollerau owns the tooling on both parts, so resourcing is easy.
The power cost decline (-43% vs 2022) undercuts any energy argument.
Our customer share is small for us, but Hollerau's spend is growing (799k), which gives them leverage on volume.
wants: A binding annual volume or a higher quota on the casing (more than 75%, forecast 1,593 pcs).
Extension of the contract by 24 months or more.
Punctual payment, or payment terms under 30 days.
An alloy index clause on AS-14404 instead of absorbing the risk ourselves.
A longer lead time (about 60 days) to fix the delivery-rate problem.
Removal or a cap on the per-complaint chargeback.
red_lines: No further cut on the casing beyond about 1% without volume or term in return.
No impeller price below about 108 EUR (no matching the CN price).
No unlimited liability for late delivery and no 95% OTD penalty clause without a lead-time adjustment.
No higher chargeback per complaint than 150 EUR.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the visit and the long partnership, and recall the 2022 price hold. Point out three years of falling prices against rising alloy and labour costs, and the zero-defect casing record. Propose holding prices flat for 2027 as our contribution, or a modest +1.5% with an alloy index clause. Offer a small impeller adjustment (around -2%) in exchange for a 24-month extension, a higher casing quota and on-time payment. Acknowledge the delivery issues and commit to an improvement plan with realistic lead times.

rebuttals.answer: You are right, and we value it: the casing quality has been excellent and we want to keep that partnership on this part. Quality is the baseline we expect from an approved supplier, though, and it does not stand alone. Delivery reliability on the same contract is well below the agreed target, and late castings stop our lines just as defects do. The casing is also the part where our forecast is rising, so we would rather reward good quality with more committed volume and a longer term than with a higher price.

We sincerely thank the owner for holding the price when it mattered, and we have not forgotten it. The renewals since then were mutual settlements reached on market evidence, not one-sided gifts, and in each of them your company landed below its own ask. We want to answer partnership with partnership: a longer commitment, binding volume where our need is firm, and punctual payment from our side. In return we ask for reliable delivery and pricing that stays competitive.

We accept that labour has risen and that the alloy surcharge is higher than a year ago. Since the summer, however, the surcharge has fallen back noticeably, and power costs are lower year on year. Weighted by their actual cost shares, the drivers net to a small movement, far from a case for an increase. The steel figure refers to basic iron and steel, not to the high-alloy grade these castings are poured from, so it does not apply here.

Fair point: the estimate is based on a different cost base and carries no margin, and we will not treat it as a German price. Even with a healthy margin and German labour added, the gap on the impeller remains wide. Your shorter lead time has real value to us, but only if the dates are met, and impeller delivery has been the weakest on the contract. We see the impeller as the part where price needs to move most.

This is a fair criticism and we accept it. We will commit to paying punctually on the agreed term as part of this agreement. We would expect the same discipline on delivery dates in return, which is where the contract target is currently not being met.

Agreed, prices are fixed per calendar year and either side may propose a change. The same clause also requires written notice before year end for any change, and the framework can be ended at the renewal point. We prefer to use the renewal to build a longer, committed partnership at competitive prices rather than simply rolling it over.

press: We would welcome a concrete plan for bringing on-time delivery back toward the agreed target, starting with the impeller.
We noticed that the recent impeller complaints had different causes, and we would appreciate a short summary of the preventive measures taken.
Since our forecast for both parts is rising and is shared with you, we would like to discuss how a binding volume and longer term could be reflected in the price.
We would appreciate your view on how the recent easing of the alloy surcharge and of power costs is reflected in your offer.
